items.title: Peppermint oil reduces blood pressure by 8.48 mmHg in small study

items.title: Membership is Ownership: A Robust Ownership Verification Framework for Diffusion Models
items.title_zh: 成员即所有权：一种面向扩散模型的鲁棒所有权验证框架
items.summary: Proposes MiO, a diffusion-model ownership verification framework built on population-level hypothesis testing over a private member evidence dataset, combining membership-inference attribution with separation from public references at p<10^-6. Evaluated on DDIM and Stable Diffusion without altering the owner model or sampling pipeline, it reports stability under post-theft fine-tuning and weight perturbation relative to watermarking baselines.

items.title: Budget-Aware Compression Pipeline for Single-GPU LLM Inference: Methods, Trade-offs, and Coupling Effects
items.title_zh: 面向单 GPU 大模型推理的预算感知压缩流水线：方法、权衡与耦合效应
items.summary: Casts single-GPU inference of 70B-parameter models as a budget-aware design problem and studies how pruning, quantization and KV-cache compression interact under realistic execution. Guided by these coupling results, it assembles a pipeline that compresses a 70B model to about 33 GB, sustains about 57 tokens/s on 10k-token prompts on a single A40, and keeps absolute accuracy within 5% on common and reasoning benchmarks.

items.title: BenchBench-Protocol: Evaluating Real-World Wet-Lab Protocol Reasoning and Modification
items.title_zh: BenchBench-Protocol：评估真实湿实验室实验方案推理与修改能力
items.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 149 protocol-modification tasks reconstructed from the changes scientists made to published wet-lab protocols, drawn from 96 source protocols across nine domains of wet-lab biology. Across nine closed and open models, Claude Opus 5 scores highest at 59.2% normalized rubric score while the others fall between 34.1% and 47.1%, and the benchmark remains unsaturated when taking the best of ten attempts.

items.title: LibriBrain100: One Hundred Hours of Broad and Deep MEG Data for Neural Speech Decoding at Scale
items.title_zh: LibriBrain100：用于大规模神经语音解码的一百小时广度与深度兼具的 MEG 数据
items.summary: Introduces a MEG dataset of over 100 hours recorded while subjects listened to naturalistic continuous speech, including about 80 hours from a single subject plus roughly 40 minutes each from 32 additional subjects. Using an existing decoding model the authors report state-of-the-art word-classification performance, and they show that supervised fine-tuning on multi-subject data can substantially compensate for limited per-subject data.

items.title: Informational Antilocality and the Locality Bias in LLMs
items.title_zh: 信息反局部性与大语言模型中的局部性偏置
items.summary: Constructs k-antilocal languages, which carry no mutual information across any span of k contiguous symbols, and trains transformer language models on them for increasing k. The models reach comparable cross-entropy loss regardless of antilocality but converge more slowly on more antilocal languages, supporting the view that non-local dependencies are harder to learn while locating the evidence in learning speed rather than learning success.

items.title: Item-Mean Surrogates: Why Richer Persona Data Fail to Improve LLMs as Human Surrogates
items.title_zh: 题目均值替代：为何更丰富的人设数据无法提升 LLM 作为人类替代品的效果
items.summary: Tests the premise that richer persona data makes LLMs better substitutes for specific individuals across four datasets covering over 400,000 participants and more than 6,000 survey items and experimental outcomes. After removing each item's human mean, LLM predictions explain only 3.05% of remaining respondent-specific variation versus a 53.6% human test-retest benchmark, and richer personas, model variants and fine-tuning do not close the gap.

items.title: When Does a Classifier Help an LLM? Classifier-Guided Prompting and Hybrid Classifier-LLM Models for Credit-Default Prediction
items.title_zh: 分类器何时能帮助 LLM？面向信用违约预测的分类器引导提示与混合分类器-LLM 模型
items.summary: Studies how a fitted classifier and an LLM can be combined for credit-default prediction, distinguishing instructing the LLM to imitate a classifier from using the classifier to build the prompt. On the Default of Credit Card Clients dataset, pruning the prompt to the classifier's eight most important features raised recall by 0.071 and F1 by 0.032, and adding the predicted probability raised the LLM's AUC-ROC from 0.72 to 0.78 while retaining higher recall than a random forest.
